solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Supporting music in reliable way

parts.note: a sound argument or investment is a reliable one
a track is a path or way

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a dependable route to the background music.
explanation.definitionFit: A film's recorded score is the music that accompanies and supports the action on screen.

clue.text: Glove puppet in which third of fingers is stuck up

indicators.note: in which tells us the next piece sits inside the puppet's name

parts.note: Sooty is a famous yellow bear glove puppet from British children's television

indicators.note: third of picks the third letter of fingers

explanation.surface: A glove puppet is stuck on someone's fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a long-running British TV glove puppet bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck up is an idiom for snobbish or haughty, which is what snooty means.

clue.text: Unmentionable things such as a zombie does apparently

definitions.meaning: unmentionables is a jokey euphemism for underwear

definitions.text: such as a zombie does apparently

explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is jokingly called unmentionables; a zombie rising from the dead could be said to un-die.

clue.text: Childish timepiece? Blow me! It's somehow conned local kid

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters being rearranged in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a local child has been tricked over a toy clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me!' looks like an exclamation of surprise but belongs to the definition: you blow a seed head to tell the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Children blow on a fluffy seed head and count puffs to 'tell the time', making it a childish clock.

clue.text: Worker caught by lefty Miliband in the act

indicators.note: caught by means the worker is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
Ed Miliband, a former UK Labour Party leader
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer is apprehended by the left-wing politician Ed Miliband.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party from 2010 to 2015.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught red-handed is an idiom meaning caught in the very act of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Long for bloke over time

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places one piece above the other

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: Someone pines for a man as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to desire something intensely, to yearn after it.

clue.text: Eastern movie spectacular

parts.note: a pic is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: A lavish film from the East is promoted as a spectacular.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand, large-scale film or show, especially one with a huge cast, is called a spectacular.

clue.text: Cable to follow for part of the country

indicators.note: to follow places the politician's name after the other piece

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Vince Cable, a former UK Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A telegraph cable is followed across a stretch of territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Cable is Vince Cable, a British Liberal Democrat politician, not a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative region or division within a nation.

clue.text: Hazard to mountaineers or cavers wandering over South-East

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places one piece above the other
wandering suggests the letters of cavers roaming into a new order

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for South-East

explanation.surface: Climbers or potholers roam about in the south-east of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier, a danger to climbers.

clue.text: Hot bearded star performing act on stage

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters putting on a show in a new order

explanation.surface: A sweaty, bearded celebrity is doing his routine in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is an idiom meaning to be an actor and appear in plays.

clue.text: Ancient celebrating fifty years without grand opening

indicators.note: without tells us to drop a letter from the anniversary word

parts.note: a golden wedding or jubilee marks fifty years

indicators.note: the opening of the word grand is its first letter

explanation.surface: An elderly couple mark their fiftieth anniversary without a lavish launch party.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective meaning belonging to times long past, i.e. ancient.

clue.text: Fish ration covering back of leaf

indicators.note: covering means the ration word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a dole is a portion handed out, a ration
the verso is the reverse side of a page or leaf of a book

explanation.surface: A small portion of food is wrapped around the underside of a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dover sole is a prized European flatfish caught in the English Channel.

clue.text: Woman will be at that point when going west

parts.note: there means at that place or point

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means read right to left

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone will reach a certain spot once they head west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' is only a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a woman's given name, as in Theresa May.

clue.text: Artisan working for empress

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of artisan being worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A craftsman toils away on behalf of the empress.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a female ruler of Russia, an empress.

clue.text: With credit after frauds, succeeded making moonshine

indicators.note: after places the credit word behind the frauds word

parts.note: fiddles are swindles or frauds
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Bootleggers using credit and swindles succeeded in producing illicit liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean foolish talk or nonsense, and fiddlesticks is an exclamation of nonsense.

clue.text: Exit scene unfortunately could put paid to it!

definitions.text: Exit scene unfortunately could put paid to it!

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of the two words coming out badly jumbled

explanation.surface: An actor's departure from the stage could prove fatal to his life.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the answer: an exit scene, a death, ends one's being.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is being alive, which a final departure from life's stage would end.

clue.text: Pawn and knight taken up in genuine act of revenge

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the genuine word

parts.note: real means genuine
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

indicators.note: in a down answer, taken up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: A chess pawn and knight are captured in a real game.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' means read upwards; the chess pieces sit inside the genuine word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is a retaliatory act, revenge for a wrong.

clue.text: Being full of oneself like inhabitant of Middle East area

parts.note: eg, for example, can stand for like
an Omani comes from Oman in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone is self-absorbed, much like a resident of a Gulf region.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is obsessive self-centredness, extreme conceit.

clue.text: Reverend I will get drunk imbibing spirit — his job's on the line

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the spirit goes inside
drunk suggests the letters of the clergyman and I staggering into a new order

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A vicar admits he will get drunk on gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get drunk' is the anagram signal, not a confession; the definition is a cryptic picture of a railwayman whose work runs along the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A train driver works on the railway line, so his job is literally on the line.

clue.text: Workforce on a Hebridean island

parts.note: the staff are the workforce of an organisation

explanation.surface: Employees are working on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are the islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: Quaker offers resistance when beset by devil

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a fiend is a devil
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A pacifist Quaker holds out when attacked by the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, so each member is a Friend.

clue.text: Fictional lawman's spurning old wrinkles

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so a letter is thrown out

parts.note: Rumpole of the Bailey is a fictional British barrister from the TV series and books, with the possessive giving S

explanation.surface: A fictional lawyer's refusal of old age shows in his lined face.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace Rumpole is the barrister hero of John Mortimer's British TV and book series Rumpole of the Bailey.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple something is to crease or crumple it, so the verb means wrinkles.

clue.text: Neat guide

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle; a castrated young bull
to direct the course of something, to pilot

explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young castrated bullock, i.e. neat cattle; to steer is also to direct a course.

clue.text: Horse to move unsteadily round run

indicators.note: round means the unsteady-movement word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to totter is to walk or move unsteadily
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A horse wobbles unsteadily around the track during its run.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is a horse bred and trained for trotting races.

clue.text: State enrolled nurse about to take top off shortly — it's essential for tanning

indicators.note: about means the nurse goes around the other piece

parts.note: SEN is the abbreviation for State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: to unscrew a jar or bottle is to take its top off

explanation.surface: A nurse is about to remove the cap of a bottle of lotion for sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the last letter of the unscrewing word; the nurse's abbreviation then wraps 'about' what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sun cream is lotion applied when sunbathing, which is the time one tans.

clue.text: Get annoyed about fellow's weapon

indicators.note: about means the annoyance word goes around the other letter

parts.note: to rile is to annoy; taken as an imperative this is the verb
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A man becomes annoyed about another man's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a weapon.

clue.text: Scoff about dishonest chap

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rail is to scoff or protest scornfully

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a dishonest fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar is someone who tells untruths, a dishonest person.

clue.text: Grassed area gardeners prepared round wicket

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
prepared suggests the letters of gardeners being made ready in a new form

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: Groundsmen get a lawn ready around the cricket wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges GARDENERS into GREENSARD, which goes 'round' W after the fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensward is an old word for turf, an area covered with grass.
